Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run-chase. The players and umpires return after the innings break. South Africa Women are in a huddle before they spread onto the field. Sarah Bryce and Saskia Horley stride out to open the batting for Scotland Women. It will be Marizanne Kapp with the ball for South Africa Women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, the target for Scotland Women is a stiff one. They need 167 runs to stay alive in the tournament. Can they pose a challenge to chase this total or will the South Africa Women bowlers prove to be too strong for them? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Darcey Carter comes in for a chat and shares her thoughts on the pitch, saying it looks good and that 160 seems like a solid total on this wicket. Mentions that she aimed to bowl a bit quicker and is thrilled to have picked up a wicket with her very first delivery. She further highlights the quality of spinners in her team and adds that she always strives to give her best in the field.

Scotland Women were below par with the ball and leaked too many runs in the powerplay. The spinners pulled things back nicely and a few tidy overs at the backend helped them stem the flow of runs. All the bowlers except for Abtaha Maqsood snapped a wicket each to complete an all-around effort from the Scottish Women.

A solid batting performance from South Africa Women helps them post the highest score of this T20 World Cup. They finished on a formidable score of 166 for 5 in their 20 overs. Opting to bat first, the openers got them off to a brilliant start by adding 64 inside 8 overs. Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits were dismissed in their 40s but set a good platform for the others. Marizanne Kapp with 43 off 24 provided the impetus to the innings while Sune Luus stuck a few lusty blows to take her side past the 165-run mark.

Just a single to finish the innings. It is a full ball, on off. Annerie Dercksen lofts it down to long on but it meets the fielder on a bounce. They cross for one. South Africa Women end their innings at 166/5.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are done with all the pre-match proceedings. The match is set to begin. Scotland Women players can be seen in a huddle, before they take the field. Soon after, Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits who stride out to open for South Africa Women. It will be Rachel Slater to start with the new ball. Here we go...
We are all set. Both the teams now stride out to the middle and line-up on the field, for their respective national anthems. It will be Scotland's first, followed by the South Africa's anthem.

Anneke Bosch from South Africa Women is up for a chat. She says that she feels special to be a part of the group. Adds that it was an amazing experience during the last World Cup and it gets even better now. Shares that she is enjoying her batting and is happy to hit far and long. Mentions that she is glad to be playing alongside Marizanne Kapp and Laura Wolvaardt. Ends by adding that the next two games are very important for them.

PITCH REPORT - Pommie Mbangwa notes that the temperature is a scorching 37°C, though it feels more like 45-50°C. The square boundaries measure 57m and 63m, suggesting a slight bias, while the straight hit down the ground is 73m. WV Raman observes that spin has dominated so far, and playing with the turn may be crucial for the batters. Raman also points out that the surface offers low bounce.

Kathryn Bryce, the Scotland Women skipper says that they need to start well and take early wickets. Adds that with the bat, they need to build partnerships and bat better. Mentions that they are going with same XI as the previous game. Ends by adding that they should be comfortable chasing something around 140.

Laura Wolvaardt, the South Africa Women skipper says that they will have a bat first. Adds that the wicket looks dry and batting first gives them the best chance of winning with runs on the board. Ends by sharing that they are going unchanged.

On the other hand, South African Women have had a mixed start with one win and one loss. They began their campaign with a convincing victory over the Women in Maroon but faced a narrow defeat to England Women in their last match. Batting first, they set a competitive target thanks to strong performances from Laura Wolvaardt and Marizanne Kapp. However, they couldn't hold on as England Women, led by Nat Sciver-Brunt, chased down the total in a tense finish. The Proteas Women will look to regain their winning momentum. Can Scotland Women pull off an upset, or will South Africa Women secure a comfortable victory? Scotland Women find themselves in a must-win situation after losing their first two matches. In their last outing, they were dominated by the West Indies Women, managing only 99 runs despite efforts from Ailsa Lister and Kathryn Bryce. Their bowlers claimed four wickets, but the West Indies Women finished the match in just 12 overs. Scotland Women will be eager to prove that they belong on this stage and put up a strong fight today.
